Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.

revision_notes: Confirmed. GSMA's September 2025 Ghana Digital Economy Report states population coverage exceeds 99% for both 3G and 4G, making Ghana the best performer for 4G coverage in West Africa; original cto.int source was a weak membership listing but the figure holds up against a fresher, authoritative source.

Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. Ghana's own regulator (NCA) puts average 1GB cost at $0.40-$0.96; against GNI per capita of $2,360 (Atlas method, GSMA 2025), a 1-2GB plan costs roughly 0.2-1.0% of monthly GNI, which meets the UN Broadband Commission's <1% target rather than the 1-2% 'Affordable' band originally scored.

revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank/ITU data (via UNdata and Trading Economics) put Ghana at 69.94% individuals using the internet in 2023, consistent with the original figure and squarely within the 50-69% band; no more recent official figure was available.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. The original 114% figure is NCA's SIM/connections penetration rate, not unique-subscriber penetration as the variable requires. GSMA's September 2025 report estimates ~21 million unique mobile users in Ghana, equivalent to about 60% of the total population, which falls in the 55-69% band rather than 70%+.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The Africa Interconnection Report 2025 shows AWS, Azure and Google Cloud African infrastructure concentrated in South Africa (Cape Town/Johannesburg), with Azure's local partner stack (via Liquid C2) covering Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Zambia and Uganda — none in Ghana — so Ghana is still served remotely rather than from a local or near-local availability zone.

revision_notes: Confirmed. ITU's GCI 2024 and Ghana's Ministry of Communications press release both verify a score of 99.27%, placing Ghana in Tier 1 (Role-Modelling), squarely in the GCI 80+ band.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The Data Protection Bill 2025 (still in draft/consultation as of May 2026 per Business & Financial Times commentary) would introduce localisation and cross-border transfer rules for sensitive categories, but the current Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843) has no such requirement, so 'proposed/draft legislation' remains accurate.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Mature framework with active enforcement and regional alignment
Comments: Mature: DPA Act 843 enacted, DPC active enforcement
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Ghana's Data Protection Commission actively enforces Act 843 (nationwide enforcement drive from August 2023), and Ghana ratified the AU Malabo Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection in 2019, supporting both the 'active enforcement' and 'regional alignment' elements of the top band.

Comments: At least one Tier III (NITA, Equinix AC1)

Baxtel's directory lists five commercial facilities in Accra (Equinix AC1, PAIX Accra, Digital Realty ACR2, Africa Data Centres ACC1, Etix Accra), and Onix Data Centres operates an Uptime Institute Tier IV-certified facility — multiple Tier III+ facilities including a Tier IV site meets the 'multiple Tier III / at least one Tier IV' band rather than 'at least one Tier III' only.

The Ghana Hubs Network (a national network body) reports over 103 innovation hubs across Ghana's 16 regions, and the US International Trade Administration independently states there are 'more than 100 tech hubs and accelerators' in Ghana (2024) — well above the 25+ threshold for a mature, vibrant ecosystem.

Definition: The size and vibrancy of the local software developer and technology professional community. Measured through proxies such as GitHub activity, Stack Overflow representation, local tech meetup groups, and developer surveys. Comments: Developing: active communities GDG, GDG etc ~1-10k
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed but flagged for human review. The original source was a curated GitHub link list, not a population estimate. The Ghana Tech Ecosystem Survey 2025 (Code & Cocktails, 286 verified respondents, up from 190+ in 2024) confirms an active but still Accra-concentrated and relatively isolated developer community (81% in Greater Accra, 34% belong to no tech community), broadly consistent with the 'Developing' band, but no authoritative absolute headcount (e.g. GitHub Innovation Graph raw figures) could be retrieved to confirm the 1,000-10,000 range precisely — recommend human review to pin down an exact estimate.

Definition: The gap between men and women in mobile internet usage or internet access. Based on the GSMA Mobile Gender Gap data or ITU gender-disaggregated ICT statistics. A smaller gap indicates more equitable access to digital opportunities.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed, marked for human review. The original GSMA source discusses women's mobile-money entrepreneurship, not a gender gap percentage, so it does not actually support 'near parity.' GSMA's Mobile Gender Gap Reports (2024/2025) do not survey Ghana individually but put the Sub-Saharan Africa mobile-internet gender gap at 32%; a secondary Techcabal article citing UN data states ~60% of Ghanaian women own smartphones versus 72% of men (a roughly 12-17% relative gap), suggesting a 'Small gap (10-19% fewer)' band. No single authoritative Ghana-specific figure was found, so this remains best-evidence rather than confirmed — recommend human review.
